offence_severity: Minimum 6 months to maximum 2 years for 498A, 10 years for 306
physical_harm: Deceased subjected to physical and mental harassment, leading to suicide by hanging
number_of_offences: Three offences charged (306, 498A, 114), two upheld (498A and 114)
key_evidence_accepted: From a perusal of the statement by the informant and other witnesses, FIR, findings of the Investigating Officer in the chargesheet as well as the statements of the deceased’s cousins recorded during investigation prima facie indicate that the deceased was subjected to physical as well as mental cruelty by her husband and in-laws.
witness_credibility: The Court found the witness statements credible and sufficient to establish strong suspicion against the accused, indicating that the deceased faced consistent physical and mental harassment by the accused.

legal_representation.accused: Tejas Barot, Sr. Adv., Shamik Shirishbhai Sanjanwala, Ms. Rhea Chokshi, Aditya Tripathi, Advs.
legal_representation.state: Ms. Swati Ghildiyal, Ms. Devyani Bhatt, Ms. Neha Singh, Advs.

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeal partly allowed, discharged from charges under Section 306 IPC, charge under Section 498A IPC upheld

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was subjected to physical and mental harassment by her husband and in-laws, which led to her suicide, thereby making out a prima facie case under sections 306, 498A, and 114 of the IPC.
defence_argument: The appellants argued that the allegations against them are baseless, there is no prima facie case under sections 306 and 498A of the IPC, and the harassment alleged did not amount to the required mens rea or direct act to instigate suicide.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for a conviction under section 306 IPC, there must be clear evidence of direct or indirect acts of incitement to commit suicide, and that mere harassment is not sufficient unless it was so compelling that the victim perceived no alternative but to take their own life.
precedent_relied_upon: U. Suvetha v. State [2009] 7 SCR 902 : (2009) 6 SCC 757; State of A.P. v. M. Madhusudhan Rao [2008] 14 SCR 1170 : (2008) 15 SCC 582; S.S. Chheena v.
